items.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
items.summary: The paper presents a method to perform high‑probability linear regression when noise has only a finite α‑moment and covariates have limited moments, by reducing the problem to finite‑variance techniques.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it enables robust regression under heavy‑tailed data, common in real‑world AI applications.

items.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
items.summary: The paper compares linear regression, RNN, and LSTM models for one‑day‑ahead S&P 500 forecasts using a 2006‑2025 dataset with fundamentals, macro, and technical features.
items.whyItMatters: It reveals which deep‑learning methods truly outperform simple models in financial time‑series forecasting.

items.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
items.summary: MemOnce introduces a scalable memory architecture that reduces GPU memory and computation overhead for long‑horizon LLM inference.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more efficient, continuous deployment of LLMs in real‑time applications.

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: The article outlines a standardized EEG feature set for classifying ADHD in youth during cognitive tasks.
items.whyItMatters: Consistent features improve AI diagnostics and research reproducibility in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Non-penetrating World Models
items.summary: The paper introduces NoPeBench to test and finds that current interactive video world models fail to prevent object penetration, revealing hidden physical knowledge.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should know these models lack reliable physics, impacting safety and realism in AI-driven simulations.

items.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
items.summary: The article explores training transformers that simultaneously learn their own layer topology, challenging the fixed architecture convention.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers may see potential for more efficient, task‑specific models and reduced manual architecture design.

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: The paper introduces a ranking-preserving coreset method to speed up evolutionary hyperparameter optimization by reducing training data size while keeping configuration rankings intact.
items.whyItMatters: It cuts HPO costs, enabling faster model tuning on large datasets for tech developers.

items.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
items.summary: The article explains how Hub-and-Spoke Optimal Transport improves long-context models by replacing dense attention with a linear graph over windows and hubs, reducing dilution and speeding up inference.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers faster, more efficient large‑scale language models with less memory and computational cost.

items.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
items.summary: The paper proves that for any partial concept class with finite VC dimension, a deterministic agnostic PAC learner can achieve optimal sample complexity O((d+log(1/δ))/ε²).
items.whyItMatters: It guarantees efficient learning guarantees for broad classes, informing algorithm design for robust AI systems.

items.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
items.summary: BioEmu2 is a generative model that rapidly produces atomically resolved biomolecular dynamics, outperforming traditional MD simulations by orders of magnitude.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, large-scale biomolecular studies, accelerating drug discovery and protein engineering.

items.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
items.summary: The paper introduces SUAF, a method for learning reward‑independent representations that capture essential statistical dependencies for zero‑shot policy improvement.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it promises faster, transferable RL without task‑specific rewards.

items.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: StereoVLM introduces binocular vision-language models that use calibrated stereo images to infer precise metric 3D spatial relationships, overcoming ambiguity in single-view VLMs.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more accurate 3D reasoning for applications like robotics and AR, where exact spatial metrics are critical.

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. items.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
items.summary: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. items.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
items.summary: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable…

items.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
items.summary: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. Learning from EHR data across institutions is valuable because representations learned at a single site may reflect local data patterns and lack generalizability, yet pooling patient-level records across institutions is often impractical because of…

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary: Sustaining user experience (UX) quality in large-scale web search requires scalable evaluation. Traditional surveys are slow and bottleneck rapid A/B testing, while automated metrics often lack the granularity to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies. To address this, we introduce the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, a novel industrial architecture for automated UX attribution. Tier 1 (Macro System)…

items.title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
items.summary: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer. We introduce TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark built on the Brazilian pathway for early autism (TEA) screening: three fictitious instruments with the structure of real ones, a multi-professional referral flow, and export to FHIR R4 with the national RNDS…

items.title: FairITR: Fairness-Aware Learning of Multicategory Individualized Treatment Rules
items.summary: Individualized treatment rules (ITRs) recommend treatment decisions based on individual characteristics and can improve treatment outcomes beyond traditional one-size-fits-all strategies. However, similar to other commonly used algorithmic decision-making methods, ITRs without considering model fairness may result in unfair decisions across groups defined by sensitive attributes, such as race or…

items.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires…
